name: Mission Tech Compass
description: No grades, no judgment. Every nonprofit we work with has a version of this. As you answer, think of a real, recent example. It takes about 6 minutes.

bands.label: Holding It Together
bands.description: Your team makes it work through sheer effort and memory. That's real commitment, and it's also what wears people out. Information lives in many places, key steps depend on who's in the office, and reports take far longer than they should. The good news: this is where a few small changes give back the most time.
nextSteps: Pick one number your board asks for and give it one home
Write down the three tasks that only one person knows how to do
Start with a Tech Foundations Audit to find your biggest time leak
Hold off on new tools until the basics feel steady

bands.label: Making It Work
bands.description: You've got pieces that work. The friction lives in the gaps between them: copying from one tool to another, chasing updates, and double-checking numbers that don't match. Your team has found workarounds, and those workarounds quietly cost hours every week.
nextSteps: Map one everyday workflow, like intake, from first contact to follow-up
Cut the most common double entry with Smarter Workflows
Bring your key numbers together with Data Clarity & Insight
Right-size your tools, but only after the cleanup

bands.label: Picking Up Speed
bands.description: The foundation is there. Most work has a home and a process. What's left is targeted: a report that still takes a day, a spreadsheet that's outgrown itself, or a handoff that depends on one person. A few focused fixes would give real time back.
nextSteps: Fix the one workflow that breaks during busy seasons
Document the systems that live in one person's head
Explore custom tools only where you're hitting real limits

bands.label: Ready to Grow
bands.description: You're in good shape. Your systems are clear, your team uses them with confidence, and your data is trustworthy. Now technology can help you do more, not just keep up: deeper insight for funders, smoother experiences for the people you serve, and room to try new things.
nextSteps: Use a Tech Foundations Audit as a strategic tune-up
Turn your data into impact stories for funders and your board
Connect your core tools so information flows on its own
Consider custom applications where off-the-shelf tools limit you

fields.name: Think about your last board or grant report. How did the numbers come together?

options.label: Someone spent days pulling from spreadsheets, inboxes and people's memories
A few hours of copying between files and chasing people for updates
Mostly from one or two systems, with some cleanup
We opened a report. Done in minutes.

fields.name: To get one key number, like people served this month, how many places does someone check?

options.label: 4 or more (spreadsheets, email, paper, someone's memory)
One place, but we double-check it
One place, and we trust it

fields.name: A funder asks something you didn't plan for, like "How many returning families came from the north county?" What happens?

options.label: Honestly, we probably couldn't answer it
We could, after a day or two of digging
We could pull it together in an hour
We could answer before the call ends

fields.name: When two files disagree about a number, what happens?

options.label: It happens a lot, and we pick the one that looks right
It's rare, and we know which one to trust
It doesn't happen. There's one source of truth.

fields.name: When a new client, volunteer or donor reaches out, how many times does their information get typed in?

options.label: 3 or more times, into different places
Once. It flows where it needs to go.

fields.name: In a typical week, how much time does each person spend re-entering, reformatting or chasing information?
How do you usually find out something fell through the cracks, like a missed follow-up or an unanswered form?
How do intake, follow-up and handoffs happen?

options.label: We have a rhythm, but things slip
A shared process most people follow
A written process our tools help us follow (reminders, checklists, automations)

fields.name: How do your everyday tools (email, spreadsheets, forms, drives, a database) fit together?

options.label: Lots of tools, and none of them talk to each other
A handful, with copy and paste between them
A few core tools, mostly connected
A tidy set that shares information

fields.name: How long does it take to find a file or record?

options.label: Depends who you ask and which drive it's in
A few minutes of searching or asking around

fields.name: What's true about the tools you pay for?

options.label: We're not sure what we pay for
A few things we keep meaning to cancel or upgrade
We review tools and costs every year

fields.name: If your go-to tech person left tomorrow, what would happen?

options.label: Real trouble. It lives in their head.
We'd scramble for a few weeks
Bumpy, but most of it is written down
Fine. Logins, steps and systems are documented.

fields.name: Who fixes tech when something breaks?

options.label: Whoever is closest, or a volunteer when they can
One staff member, on top of their real job
Someone on staff or outside help we can call
A clear support plan, in-house or with a partner

fields.name: How do people feel about the tools they use?

options.label: A couple of people do the tech heavy lifting for everyone
Comfortable after a reminder or two
Confident, and they ask when they're stuck

fields.name: When someone leaves, how quickly do they lose access to email, drives and systems?

options.label: Honestly, not sure they all have

options.label: All over: email, laptops, shared spreadsheets
